link.title: The two-room single-photon link
link.summary: Weak 405 nm pulses at 0.5 photons, four polarization states, decoy pulses, four SiPMs, planned FPGA gating, an enclosed free-space path between the rooms; a separate fiber carries only the classical channel. The planning model predicts clicks, errors, and a test key before you buy a part (model outputs, not measurements).
bom: Two fiber media converters and a 10–30 m duplex patch cord
Four 405 nm laser diodes (5 mW class) with a nanosecond pulse driver
Film polarizers, a half-wave retarder, neutral-density filters (OD 1–4)
Four non-polarizing beamsplitters and two polarizing beamsplitters
Four onsemi MicroFC-30035 SiPMs, breakouts, a 30 V boost module, four fast comparators
Two small FPGA boards (planned; gateware not yet implemented)
A coaxial cable or second fiber for the pulse clock
3D-printed mounts, black tubes, lens pairs, black card, felt
stages: Predict the bench and write a synthetic run ($0).
Laptops, media converters, fiber through the door (M1.1).
Tier 1 through the enclosed path between the rooms (M1.3); an analogue, not secure QKD.
SiPMs, comparators, dark box; measure dark counts (M1.4).
Four diodes, polarizers, combiners, filters to μ = 0.5 (M1.5).
Passive basis choice, PBS arms, waveplate at 22.5°.
Clock over coax, gated counting, logs, twin check (M1.6).
Optional intercept-resend station inside the enclosed path.

stages: Sliders compose five channels in order.

channel.title: The hallway, certified and mapped as a quantum channel
channel.summary: The P10 link, seen as a quantum channel: the BB84 error rates certify it is not a classical relay, two quarter-wave plates add the third direction for full tomography, and the measured map gives what the hallway can carry: bits, qubits, and secret key.
bom: The two-room P10 build (see the two-room lab)
Two quarter-wave retarders cut from one film sheet, and a printed flip mount
a circular input and a circular measurement
stages: No new parts: e_Z and e_X bound the entanglement fidelity.
Quarter-wave plate behind the 45° polarizer: that diode sends R.
Flip a quarter-wave plate into the X arm: it measures Y.
Four ten-second sessions, every click logged as input, basis, outcome.
